FINAL OWNER LOGIN RECOVERY — COMPLETE NOW END TO END

CURRENT STATUS

OWNER LOGIN: FAILED
PRODUCTION STATUS: PARTIAL
SESSION REVOCATION: NOT VERIFIED
FINAL APK DEVICE QA: NOT COMPLETE

Do not return another narrative report.
Do not mark VERIFIED until the real phone test passes.

==================================================
STEP 1 — COMPLETE SECURE PASSWORD RESET
==================================================

1. Trigger the official Supabase password reset email.
2. If rate-limited, retry after the limit clears.
3. Owner sets a new private password directly through the secure reset page.
4. Do not ask the owner to paste the new password into chat.
5. Do not print, log, store, or screenshot the new password.
6. Confirm the old exposed password returns invalid_credentials.
7. Confirm the new password succeeds through the real production login screen.

Required proof:
- reset email sent timestamp
- reset link accepted
- old password rejected
- new password accepted
- owner user ID returned
- production Supabase project reference

==================================================
STEP 2 — FIX SESSION REVOCATION WARNING
==================================================

The previous admin logout test returned 404.

Do not leave this as a warning.

Determine the correct supported Supabase Auth method for the current GoTrue version.

Verify all three behaviors:

A. Local logout
- supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' })
- local access token removed
- local refresh token removed
- protected screens blocked

B. Global logout
- use the supported global sign-out/revocation method
- confirm all refresh tokens for the owner are invalidated where supported

C. Server-side admin session invalidation
- use the correct Supabase Admin API or supported SDK method
- do not call a nonexistent endpoint
- if the current project/version does not support a specific endpoint, document the supported replacement

Required proof:
- exact SDK/API method
- exact source file
- HTTP status
- refresh-token reuse test
- old session accepted or rejected
- result on same device
- result on second session/device if available

PASS CONDITION:
After logout, the previous session cannot reopen owner routes.
After global revocation, an old refresh token cannot create a new session.

==================================================
STEP 3 — TEST THE EXACT PHONE LOGIN PATH
==================================================

Use only the exact real app flow:

supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({
  email: normalizedEmail,
  password: userEnteredPassword
})

Do not use:
- service-role tokens
- admin-generated tokens
- magic links
- existing sessions
- server-side credential grant
- test fixtures
- mocked responses
- password injection

Test on the physical Android phone:

1. Uninstall previous IVX app.
2. Clear previous application data.
3. Install the newest production APK.
4. Open the app.
5. Verify app version and commit.
6. Enter owner email manually.
7. Enter the new private password manually.
8. Tap Sign In.
9. Confirm HTTP 200/session returned.
10. Confirm owner user ID.
11. Open Owner Dashboard.
12. Open Admin Hub.
13. Open Settings.
14. Open Variables.

Required proof:
- device model
- Android version
- APK version
- versionCode
- source commit
- production Supabase project reference
- safe auth log
- screen recording with password hidden

==================================================
STEP 4 — COMPLETE OWNER AUTHENTICATION QA
==================================================

Run these tests one by one:

1. Correct password login
2. Wrong password rejection
3. Missing password rejection
4. Logout
5. Login again
6. Kill app and reopen
7. Session persistence
8. Expired-token refresh
9. Local logout blocks protected pages
10. Global revocation invalidates old session
11. Non-owner login
12. Non-owner Owner Dashboard rejection
13. Non-owner Admin Hub rejection
14. Non-owner Settings rejection
15. Non-owner Variables rejection
16. Password reset
17. Old password rejected after reset
18. New password accepted
19. Passwordless login does not alter password flow
20. No unauthorized automatic login

Return:

Test | Expected | Actual | HTTP status | User role | Result | Evidence

PASS CONDITION:
All 20 tests pass on production.

==================================================
STEP 5 — REMOVE THE PASSWORDLESS CONFLICT
==================================================

Audit and isolate:

- password login
- magic-link login
- OTP login
- deep-link session recovery
- cached sessions
- Remember Me
- auto-login
- password reset state

Rules:

- Password login must call signInWithPassword only.
- Magic-link state must never overwrite password state.
- OTP state must never overwrite password state.
- Remember Me stores only the intended session behavior, never the password.
- Logout clears local authentication state.
- Invalid sessions return to login.
- No hidden test password or hardcoded password remains.

Search entire repository and history-sensitive working files for:
- passwords
- service-role keys
- owner tokens
- hardcoded credentials
- test fixtures containing secrets

Return:
- files checked
- findings
- files corrected
- zero-secret verification result

==================================================
STEP 6 — FIX THE SECURITY EXPOSURE COMPLETELY
==================================================

The previous report says a service-role key had been hardcoded.

Complete the security remediation:

1. Remove the key from source.
2. Remove it from current working files.
3. Rotate the Supabase service-role key.
4. Update the new key only in secure server-side secrets.
5. Confirm mobile/web bundles do not contain the key.
6. Confirm GitHub Actions logs do not expose it.
7. Confirm Render environment uses the rotated key.
8. Confirm old key returns 401/403.
9. Confirm new server-side key works.
10. Add automated secret scanning.

Required proof:
- rotation timestamp
- affected services updated
- old key rejected
- new key verified
- repository secret scan result
- APK bundle scan result
- web bundle scan result

Do not expose either key in the report.

==================================================
STEP 7 — BUILD A NEW FINAL APK
==================================================

Because authentication and security changed, create a new APK.

Requirements:

- correct production Supabase project
- correct production API
- no Expo Go
- no Rork branding
- no localhost
- no temporary URLs
- no hardcoded credentials
- release signing
- incremented version
- incremented versionCode
- universal APK
- SHA-256 checksum
- owner-controlled GitHub Release
- direct APK asset URL

Return:

APK filename:
App version:
Version code:
Package ID:
Source commit:
EAS build ID:
Build status:
File size:
SHA-256:
GitHub Release URL:
Direct APK URL:
EAS artifact URL:

Do not reuse the previous APK as final proof.

==================================================
STEP 8 — PHYSICAL ANDROID FINAL QA
==================================================

Install the new APK on the real phone and test:

1. Fresh install
2. First launch
3. Owner login
4. Owner Dashboard
5. Admin Hub
6. Settings
7. Variables
8. Logout
9. Protected routes blocked
10. Login again
11. Kill/reopen
12. Session persists
13. Wrong password rejected
14. Non-owner rejected
15. Members load
16. Investors load
17. Buyers load
18. Properties load
19. Investment cards load
20. Reels play
21. Chat opens
22. Keyboard works
23. Messages persist
24. Image upload
25. Video upload
26. Document upload
27. Notifications
28. Background/resume
29. Network interruption/recovery
30. No crash or infinite loader

Required proof:
- full screen recording
- device details
- APK details
- test timestamps
- pass/fail matrix
- crash logs for failures

==================================================
STEP 9 — VERIFY PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

Return direct proof:

- active GitHub repository
- branch
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Render service
- Render deployment ID
- Render deployment status
- Render deployed SHA
- /health SHA
- build version
- boot time
- HTTP 200
- GitHub SHA == Render SHA == /health SHA

Do not infer deployment status only from a report.
Query Render directly using the stored credential.

If Render access fails:
- show exact variable checked
- exact request
- exact HTTP status
- exact error
- only then request correction

==================================================
STEP 10 — FINAL ACCEPTANCE GATE
==================================================

Mark VERIFIED only when all are true:

- password reset completed
- old exposed password rejected
- new password works on real phone
- owner routes open
- wrong password rejected
- non-owner rejected
- local logout works
- global session revocation works
- passwordless flow no longer interferes
- service-role key rotated
- no secrets remain in source/bundles
- new production APK delivered
- physical Android QA passes
- GitHub, Render, and /health SHAs match
- no critical authentication failure remains

Final output must include:

OWNER LOGIN STATUS:
SESSION REVOCATION STATUS:
SECURITY ROTATION STATUS:
ANDROID APK STATUS:
PHYSICAL DEVICE QA STATUS:
PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT STATUS:
FINAL STATUS:

Use:
VERIFIED
only after every critical gate passes.

Otherwise use:
PARTIAL
or
BLOCKED

Do not ask whether to proceed.
Start now with password reset, session revocation, secret rotation, new APK build, and physical phone QA.
